title: perf-bench-sync-sprint-11
content:
Perf & Benchmark Sync notes — Sprint 11 (10 Mar 2026)

Attendees: Aisha (owner), Marcus, Priya, Evan, Tomás, SRE on-call (brief).
Meeting length: 40m. Quick standup-style updates then deep-dive on the 99th pct latency regression observed on Wednesday night.

Summary of problem:
- Incident: Wednesday 2026-03-04 23:10 UTC, hosted inference fleet for rdx-7b-qat showed 99p latency jump from ~210ms -> ~510ms under steady-state traffic on region-eu.
- Throughput reported drop: observed qps per replica decreased ~22% on the affected pool. CPU on frontend proxies spiked; GPU utility dropped ~8%.
- Regression window correlates with a patch deployment to kernel-selection optimizer (PR #1876) that rolled out across dedicated routing nodes.

Quick hypothesis list (prioritized):
1) Kernel chooser fallbacks to slower FP path for certain sequence lengths due to heuristic mis-match after change in PR #1876.
2) KV-cache invalidation logic causing repeated recomputation for popular prefixes (cache version bump race).
3) Autoscaler backoff policy combined with a scoring change in the routing policy made fewer warm replicas available.

Repro & local bench steps (commands used by team):
- Repro script (local): ./bench/run_local.sh --model rdx-7b-qat --seq 1024 --batch 1 --tokens 512 --profile kernel,kv --duration 300
- Cloud repro job: gcloud ai-platform jobs submit --config bench-config-7b.yaml --job-name repro-7b-20260305
- Key perf command to collect traces: DEBUG=runtime:trace ./serving-client --target pool-eu --profile=trace --duration=180

Collected observations from repro runs:
- When forcing kernel selector to choose FP16-path explicitly (overriding new heuristic), latency returns to baseline (~215ms p99).
- KV cache eviction counters show a 3x increase in miss-rate in the night window on repro cluster when we enable the new selector.
- Autoscaler logs show scale-downs happening 20–30s sooner than pre-change; cold-start latency measured at ~1.1s per new replica, contributing to tail.

Immediate conclusions so far:
- Root cause likely interaction between kernel-selection fallback and KV cache behavior. The new kernel heuristic misclassifies certain prompt shapes that cause the runtime to recompile or select suboptimal kernels, increasing per-token compute and increasing KV misses (because path differences change cache keys).
- Autoscaler policy exacerbates by reducing warm capacity; combined effect yields higher p99.

Experiment matrix (planned):
1) Roll PR #1876 temporarily back on one canary region and run same load — metric: p99 latency, p50, qps, cache-miss-rate. Owner: Priya. Deadline: 2026-03-12 18:00 UTC.
2) Add targeted override in kernel selector to force FP16 for sequence lengths 512–2048 and run bench-suite. Owner: Marcus. Deadline: 2026-03-13 EOD.
3) Increase autoscaler warm window by +45s for pool-eu as an emergency short-term mitigation. Owner: Evan. Deadline: 2026-03-11 09:00 UTC.
4) Add KV-cache metrics (per-prefix hit/miss) to the runtime exposer for 48h to capture pattern. Owner: Tomás. Deadline: 2026-03-11 12:00 UTC.

Action items recorded (with owners):
- Priya: revert PR #1876 on canary routing nodes and run smoke + bench. Ping when done (JIRA INF-3450).
- Marcus: produce a targeted kernel-selector override patch and bench matrix for seq lengths [128,512,1024,2048]. Add notes on whether quantized kernels differ.
- Evan: change autoscale policy on pool-eu to prefer maintaining 2 warm replicas(extra) until midnight UTC for the next 3 days; monitor cost delta.
- Tomás: instrument KV-cache exports, upload to S3 (s3://redwood-bench/perf/2026-03-10/). Provide Grafana dashboard link in JIRA.
- Aisha: consolidate results, write postmortem draft if regression confirmed, coordinate comms to customer-success for impacted tenants.

Observability & thresholds to add (agreed):
- Add alert: kv_cache.miss_rate > 0.1 for 5m at pool-level.
- Alert: p99_latency_delta > 100ms sustained for 10m.
- Add tracing tag to requests that trigger kernel selector fallback (enable sampling 5%).

Notes from standup snippets:
- Marcus: saw that quantized 4-bit kernels behave differently; need to test both q4 and q8 paths explicitly.
- Priya: rollback on canary completed, preliminary numbers show p99 dropped ~70ms on canary. Running full suite overnight.
- Evan: autoscaler change staged to prod playbook; cost impact estimated +6% for pool-eu, fine for 48h emergency.
- Tomás: added per-prefix cache histograms to the exporter; initial heatmap shows 6 prefixes responsible for 65% of misses.

Follow-ups for next sync (2026-03-13 10:00 UTC):
- Priya to present canary vs control bench graphs.
- Marcus to share override patch and quick perf run.
- Tomás to present Grafana heatmap & S3 artifact path.
- Aisha to propose wording for customer comms if we need a customer-facing postmortem.

Notes / rough TODO: (freeform)
- Investigate whether the kernel heuristic change included any implicit changes to cache keys (stringified shapes). If so, we may need a migration shim.
- Check PR #1876 changelog for any logging-level changes — might have inadvertently increased logging (I/O) on routing nodes.
- Prepare a short-run test that simulates popular prefixes from heatmap to validate patch quickly.

Attached artifacts / logs locations referenced in meeting: 
- Repro job artifacts: gs://bench-results/repro-7b-20260305/
- Detailed traces: s3://redwood-traces/pool-eu/2026-03-04/trace-*.json
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1876
- JIRA: INF-3421 (regression triage), INF-3450 (revert & canary)

End of notes.

-- Aisha Khatri (on behalf of eng-serving-runtime)
